e: Kenya reports its first ever Ebola case following the death of a patient in Nairobi who had traveled to the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.
A road accident at Salama along the Nairobi–Mombasa Highway in Makueni County kills 17 and injures seven, mostly Catholic pilgrims, that were travelling for a National Prayer Day.
Groundbreaking of the planned Ksh.2 trillion (about $16 billion) Dangote East Africa Refinery.
Jebet Ngetich breaks the women-only half-marathon world record by one second, running 1:05:15 at the World Athletics Road Running Championships in Copenhagen.
Four people are killed and at least 22 others seriously injured while attempting to siphon fuel from a petrol tanker involved in an accident in Turbo Constituency, Uasin Gishu County.
Five people including two Anti-Stock Theft Unit (ASTU) officers and a National Police Reserve officer are ambushed and killed in Gotu, Isiolo County.

The High Court upholds that former presidents are legally barred from being leaders of political parties six months after they leave office. This leads to Uhuru Kenyatta vacating the leadership of the Jubilee Party on 15 September.
President Ruto orders the departure of Tata Chemicals from Kenya, accusing the firm of exporting soda ash from the country instead of processing it domestically.
Ruto orders a crackdown on foreigners working in small retail shops and hawking, leading to the alleged harassment and violence against foreigners in those jobs.
A forest fire breaks out at Mount Kenya Forest, consuming 30,000 acres of moorland by 7 September.

The Kenya Aviation Workers Union (KAWU) resumes its previously suspended strike due to alleged lack of government implementation of the Memorandum of Understanding that ended the previous strike. It results in flight disruptions across the nation's airports including at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.

Seven people are killed when an Eurocopter EC130 B4 carrying tourists crashes at Mount Ololokwe, Samburu County whilst flying to the Loisaba Conservancy. The victims include five American citizens and Ecuadorian intelligence chief Michele Sensi-Contugi.
Agence France-Presse and The Associated Press
Four people are killed during a Linda Mwananchi political rally in Homa Bay.
Nairobi formally submits its bid to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships, with the Kenyan government providing full backing.

Nurses across the country begin a months long strike triggered by grievances dating back to 2017, with the Kenya National Union of Nurses (KNUN) accusing the government of refusing to address any of the problems facing Kenyan nurses and citing the strike as a last resort. It ends after the Council of Governors signs a 9 September return to work formula with them.
Former Migori County Governor Okoth Obado, his former Personal Assistant Michael Oyamo and former Migori County Clerk Caspal Obiero are found guilty of the 2018 murder of Sharon Otieno.
The Law Society of Kenya boycotts multiple Kenyan courts in protest to corruption, judicial misconduct and delayed justice, citing the need for accountability and reforms in the judiciary.
Ol Kalou Constituency by-election: Sammy Kamau Waweru of the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) wins his first National Assembly seat.
Middle-distance runner Emmanuel Wanyonyi sets a new men's 1,000 metres world record of 2:11.83 at the Herculis, breaking the previous record of 2:11.96 set by fellow countryman Noah Ngeny in 1999.
Edwin Sifuna is officially removed as the secretary general of the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM).
The High Court orders the recomposition of President Ruto's Cabinet due to it breaking the two-thirds gender rule.

One person is killed while two others are injured by gunfire in Mathare during demonstrations demanding the release of allegedly abducted protesters demanding justice for those killed and injured during the 2024 Finance Bill protests.
Three people die from asphyxia in a sewer trench in Riruta Satellite, Nairobi after the first man got stuck while unblocking it and two other colleagues entered it in a failed rescue attempt.
Kenya begins repatriation of its citizens fleeing anti-immigrant protests in South Africa. The repatriates are escaping threats of violence, including physical attacks on them or their businesses.
Annual Lewa Safari Marathon organized by Tusk.

Former half marathon world record holder Kibiwott Kandie is banned by the Athletics Integrity Unit for seven years, after being found guilty of refusing to provide a doping sample and tampering with the doping control process.
The High Court finds Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale in contempt of court for failing to comply with orders halting construction of a U.S.-backed Ebola quarantine facility at Laikipia Air Base.
The 11th Our Ocean Conference is held in Mombasa and Kilifi County.
The government announces compensation payments to 2,000 victims of human rights abuses related to protests.

The Switzerland-based Legal Action Worldwide, representing victims of the Sudanese civil war (2023–present), files a complaint against the Rapid Support Forces in Kenya for war crimes, marking the first such legal action against the group outside Sudan.
Former chief justice David Maraga is briefly arrested while participating in a protest against construction works inside Nairobi National Park.
Kenya hosts the World Rafting Championship at Sagana, Kirinyaga County.
A nganya matatu performing a stunt at Industrial Area, Nairobi, overturns and kills five people, leaving 12 seriously injured.
Two people are shot dead during a protest in Nanyuki against a proposed United States-backed Ebola quarantine facility intended for asymptomatic Americans exposed to the virus.
The High Court suspends a US plan to establish a quarantine facility in Kenya for American citizens exposed abroad to ebolavirus.
Sixteen children are killed in a fire at a boarding school in Gilgil. Authorities subsequently arrest eight students on suspicion of involvement in the alleged arson attack.
Fuel price hike protests resume after a week's pause, leaving one person shot dead by the police in Nyeri.
The Kenya Wildlife Marathon and Half-Marathon takes place.
The High Court decriminalizes consensual under-age sexual relationships following a case involving the arrest of a 17-year old minor found living with his 16-year-old partner.

Four people are killed, transportation paralyzed and more than 30 injured during nationwide protests and a public transport strike over sharp fuel price increases, linked to global supply pressures caused by the 2026 Iran war.
